package.name: search
package.packageFile:
# FULLY DECLARATIVE. Six nodes, one endpoint, one key.
#
# SearchAPI.io is the cleanest case for this format: every engine is the SAME url switched
# by `engine=`, authenticated by one `api_key` in the query. `shared/searchapi.yaml` holds
# the call, each node names its engine and shapes its own reply, and the whole client is
# gone: `auth: apiKeyQuery` was already an executor capability.
#
# The retired TypeScript is at `_legacy/nodes/search/`.

name: search
displayName: Search
description: Web, news, video, places, one place's listing and by-image search via SearchAPI.io
version: 2.0.0
category: search
logoUrl: https://cdn-icons-png.flaticon.com/512/3128/3128287.png

features:
  - Google web and image results
  - Google News, dated articles
  - YouTube video search
  - Google Maps places with ratings
  - One Google Maps listing in full, photos and facts, by place id
  - Google Lens, the pages a picture appears on

allowedHosts:
  - www.searchapi.io

requires:
  credential: [apiKeyQuery]
  transport: [json]
  executorVersion: ">=1.0.0"

credentials.searchapiCredential.yaml:
# One key powers every engine in this package. Transcribed from src/credentials/index.ts.

name: searchapiCredential
displayName: SearchAPI
description: SearchAPI.io credentials. One key powers every search engine in this package.
documentationUrl: https://www.searchapi.io/docs

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your SearchAPI.io API key
    placeholder: ""

shared.searchapi.yaml:
# The ONE call every node in this package makes.
#
# Same url, same auth, switched by `engine`. A node $refs this and layers its own `query`
# keys on top, which is what a $ref with siblings does: imported first, local wins.
#
# The key travels as a query parameter because that is what the vendor takes. `apiKeyQuery`
# is an executor capability, so no node handles a secret itself.

call: &call
  method: GET
  url: https://www.searchapi.io/api/v1/search
  credential:
    scheme: apiKeyQuery
    param: api_key
    value: "{{ credentials.searchapiCredential.apiKey }}"
  headers:
    Accept: application/json
  transport: json
  retry:
    attempts: 3
    backoff: exponential
    on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504]

# A 200 is not always a success here: the vendor reports a bad parameter or an exhausted
# quota in the body. Without this a failed search emits empty results and reads as "nothing
# found", which is the wrong answer rather than an error.
#
# Except "nothing found" itself: the vendor reports an empty search in the same field
# ("Google didn't return any results."). That IS the answer, so it emits empty lists, and a
# search for a person with no news does not end the run.
error: &error
  when: "return !!response.error && !String(response.error).includes(\"didn't return any results\")"
  message: "return typeof response.error === 'string' ? response.error : JSON.stringify(response.error)"

files.api/events.yaml:
# `response` is the whole reply; the listing is its `place_result`. With no place id the call was
# skipped and both rows read an empty listing: an empty object and an empty list, never a failure.
#
# `type` is a single string on some listings and a `types` array on others, as in the places
# search. Hotel listings carry `price` (a nightly rate) and `hotel_stars` ("4 stars"); others
# carry `price` as a level ("$$$$") or nothing. The reply has NO opening hours for the place
# itself (2026-10-23, vendor docs): hours ride on the places SEARCH results, not on the listing.
- emit: place
  from: response
  value: >-
    return ((p) => ({
      placeId: p.place_id || "",
      title: p.title || "",
      description: p.description || "",
      address: p.address || "",
      phone: p.phone || "",
      website: p.website || "",
      rating: typeof p.rating === "number" ? p.rating : null,
      reviews: typeof p.reviews === "number" ? p.reviews : null,
      price: p.price || "",
      hotelStars: p.hotel_stars || "",
      type: p.type || (Array.isArray(p.types) ? p.types[0] : "") || "",
      types: Array.isArray(p.types) ? p.types : (p.type ? [p.type] : []),
      amenities: Array.isArray(p.amenities) ? p.amenities : [],
      features: Array.isArray(p.features) ? p.features : [],
      extensions: Array.isArray(p.extensions) ? p.extensions : [],
      thumbnail: p.thumbnail || "",
      gpsCoordinates: p.gps_coordinates
        ? { latitude: p.gps_coordinates.latitude, longitude: p.gps_coordinates.longitude }
        : null
    }))((response || {}).place_result || {})

# Google hands back small thumbnails; the size in the URL is raised so a card can draw a hero
# from it. The listing's own cover picture leads when the gallery does not already open with it.
- emit: images
  from: response
  value: >-
    return ((p) => {
      const big = (u) => String(u || "").replace(/=w\d+-h\d+[^&]*/, "=w1200-h800");
      const list = (Array.isArray(p.images) ? p.images : [])
        .filter(i => i && i.thumbnail)
        .map(i => ({ title: i.title || "", url: big(i.thumbnail) }));
      const cover = p.thumbnail && !list.some(i => i.url === big(p.thumbnail))
        ? [{ title: p.title || "", url: big(p.thumbnail) }] : [];
      return cover.concat(list).slice(0, config.maxImages);
    })((response || {}).place_result || {})
files.api/run.yaml:
# NO ID, NO CALL: an empty place id skips the lookup and the node answers an empty place,
# rather than failing the run it sits in (the vendor refuses a details request without one).

- $ref: searchapi#call
  name: details
  when: "return String(config.placeId || '').trim().length > 0"
  error: { $ref: searchapi#error }
  query:
    engine: google_maps_place
    place_id: "{{ config.placeId }}"
    hl: "{{ config.language }}"
files.config.yaml:
configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [placeId]
  properties:
    placeId:
      type: string
      title: Place ID
      description: The Google Maps place id to look up, e.g. 'ChIJhRwB-yFawokR5Phil-QQ3zM'. Usually wired in from a places search.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    maxImages:
      type: number
      title: Number of Photos
      description: How many of the listing's photos to return
      default: 10
      minimum: 0
      maximum: 50
    language:
      type: string
      title: Language
      description: Language code for the listing text, e.g. 'en', 'ar'
      default: en
"ui:order": [placeId, maxImages, language]
files.interface.yaml:
inputs:
  - name: placeId
    type: string
    description: Google Maps place id, as a places search returns it
    required: false

outputs:
  - name: place
    type: object
    description: >-
      The listing: title, description, address, phone, website, rating, reviews, price,
      hotelStars, type, types, amenities, openState, hours, gpsCoordinates, placeId
  - name: images
    type: array
    description: The listing's photos, each { title, url }, largest first

credentials:
  - name: searchapiCredential
    required: true
    displayName: SearchAPI
files.node.yaml:
type: SearchPlaceDetails
kind: PromiseNode
name: Search Place Details
category: Search
color: "#34A853"
logoUrl: https://cdn-icons-png.flaticon.com/512/684/684908.png
description: One place's full Google Maps listing by its place id via SearchAPI.io
whenToUse: >
  Pick to fill in ONE KNOWN PLACE from its Google Maps listing: its photos, description,
  amenities, price level, hotel stars, rating, address and coordinates. It starts from a
  place id a search already found and returns that one listing in full; it does not search
  for places, and opening hours are not part of a listing.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # Idempotent read by id: the same listing yields the same photos and facts, so a prior
  # output may be reused instead of asking again (EXECUTION_EFFICIENCY.md §3.2).
  cacheable: true
files.test.yaml:
# The vendor's own documentation example: Madison Square Garden.
testData:
  config:
    placeId: ChIJhRwB-yFawokR5Phil-QQ3zM
    maxImages: 10
    language: en
  inputs:
    placeId: ChIJhRwB-yFawokR5Phil-QQ3zM
  expect:
    place: "return typeof output.place.title === 'string' && output.place.title.length > 0 && output.place.gpsCoordinates !== null"
    images: "return Array.isArray(output.images) && output.images.length > 0 && typeof output.images[0].url === 'string'"
